basis: The dashes under the next unit (the long stroke) mark its cell, which starts at x = 219.7 pt, 2.5 pt after the right edge of the patch (217.2 pt). Signs sit in cells at least 14 pt wide, set 2.2 pt apart, and the dashes of an underline span the cell. The printed sign list (page 21, entries 397/597, 397/13, 398/598 and 398/542) draws the narrow patch at the left end of its cell for 597 and 13 and at the right end for 598 and 542, and the underlined patches in running text (13 on pages 37, 38, 75, 123 and 177; 542 on pages 75 and 177) keep exactly those offsets. The patch therefore ends where its cell ends, which is the 598 position. A patch at the left end of its cell (597) would put the next cell near 227 pt. Reader A kept both codes because a blank gap lies on the patch's left; the right-hand neighbour decides the side whatever lies on the left.

The patch (x 168.8 to 175.2 pt) is the first unit of the row and the trapezoid sign follows with its first ink at 179.8 pt. On the chart that sign's ink begins 2.7 pt inside its cell, so its cell starts near 177.1 pt, 1.9 pt after the patch. The cell geometry is the one described in N001. That fits a patch at the right end of its cell (598). A patch at the left end of its cell (597) would put the next ink near 188 pt. Reader A kept both codes because the patch starts the row; the gap to its right-hand neighbour fixes the side.

Reader A read these Y signs as plain Y.

A single tick 1.9 pt tall stands at the top of the line, with a 0.6 pt blob at tick-top height 2.4 pt to its left. The tick pair on the chart (code 25) has a spacing of 2.4 pt, and the tick here is itself shorter than the chart's 2.3 pt, so the blob may be the remains of the left tick of a pair. It may equally be a speck beside a single tick (code 23). The source does not decide, so both codes stay in the strict set. The tick sits in the top part of the line, so the centred codes are excluded. Reader A left the set empty; reader B read a pair.

decision: median of reader A, reader B and the adjudicator's own detection of the number blocks
basis: Both readers found the same row count in every column (1,847 rows in 52 columns) and located the centre of each number and classification block. Their centres differ by 1.25 pt at most and by 0.069 pt on average; 8 of 1847 rows differ by more than 0.5 pt and 3 by more than 1.0 pt. The adjudicator located the digit lines of every block independently on the page scan and found the same row count in every column. Those centres lie within 1.0 pt of reader A's for 1,839 rows and of reader B's for 1,834 rows; the exceptions, up to 3.4 pt away, are eight rows whose digit cluster picked up a stray mark. The reference takes the median of the three values for each row: it lies within 0.44 pt of reader A's centre for every row and within 0.62 pt of the mean of A and B.
